Package com.charitymap.service

Class RandomGenerator

java.lang.Object
com.charitymap.service.RandomGenerator
public class RandomGenerator extends Object
Generates entities at random positions, to satisfy the "mass add with random positions" requirement of the specification.

Positions are drawn inside a rectangular area meant to represent the city of Cergy. The bounds are kept simple on purpose so the team fully controls them.

Author:
CharityMap team

  • Method Details

    • addRandomBeneficiaries

      public void addRandomBeneficiaries(CharityMap map, int count)
      Adds a specified number of beneficiaries at random pixel coordinates within the defined generator's area.

      Each beneficiary is assigned a random AidType. This method uses the legacy internal pixel coordinate system.

      Parameters:
      map - the map that will receive the newly created beneficiaries
      count - the number of beneficiaries to generate and add

    • addRandomBeneficiariesInBounds

      public void addRandomBeneficiariesInBounds(CharityMap map, int count, double minLng, double maxLng, double minLat, double maxLat, BiFunction<Double,Double,Point> projection)
      Adds a given number of beneficiaries at random positions inside the specified latitude/longitude bounding box.

      For each beneficiary, the method chooses a random aid type, generates a uniformly distributed point inside the provided bounds, and converts the resulting geographic coordinates into the map's internal coordinate system by applying the supplied projection function.

      Parameters:
      map - the map that will receive the newly created beneficiaries
      count - the number of beneficiaries to generate
      minLng - the minimum longitude of the bounding box
      maxLng - the maximum longitude of the bounding box
      minLat - the minimum latitude of the bounding box
      maxLat - the maximum latitude of the bounding box
      projection - a function used to convert the generated latitude/longitude coordinates into a Point on the map
